help.intro: Jan leaves Lisa a voicemail proposing a plan for Saturday: what, when, why, how much it costs, where to meet, and what to bring. Heard only. A voicemail with a proposal is one of the most common messages a friend leaves you, and the questions map onto its parts: the activity (an exhibition), the reason (weil … verb at the end), the price (with an aber that changes it), the meeting place (vor dem Museum — a two-way preposition, dative because it is a position), and the request at the end (bring bitte … mit). Listen for the shape of a suggestion — Wir können …, Treffen wir uns …? — and catch each weil-clause to the end, because the verb that closes it names the reason.
help.tips[0].title: The reason is after weil, to the end of the clause
help.tips[0].text: …, weil es dann nicht so voll ist — the reason is 'not so full', and the verb ist closes it. Hold the clause to its last word.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: We can go at three, because it's not so crowded then.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: I think you'll like it, because you're so interested in photography.
help.tips[0].check.q: You hear: „Ich komme später, weil mein Zug Verspätung hat.“ Why is the speaker late?
help.tips[0].check.why: The reason runs from weil to the verb hat at the end: mein Zug hat Verspätung — the train is late.
help.tips[1].title: How a plan is proposed
help.tips[1].text: Ich wollte dich fragen, ob du Zeit hast · Wir können … · Treffen wir uns …? · Oder soll ich dich abholen? · Danach … · Ruf mich zurück. The shape is always the same; the details change.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: Shall we meet at a quarter to three in front of the museum? Or shall I pick you up by car?
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: Please call me back, or send me a message.
help.tips[1].check.q: ____ wir uns um acht am Bahnhof? (Shall we meet …?)
help.tips[1].check.why: A suggestion with wir puts the verb first in the wir-form: Treffen wir uns …?
help.tips[2].text: The meeting place uses a two-way preposition in its position sense: vor dem (not vor das) — nobody moves, they just stand there.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: Shall we meet at a quarter to three in front of the museum?
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: … a coffee in the café next to the museum.
help.tips[2].check.q: Wir treffen uns vor ____ Kino. (meeting place: das Kino)
help.tips[2].check.why: The meeting place is a position, nobody moves into the cinema, so vor takes the dative: vor dem Kino.
help.tips[3].title: aber changes the number
help.tips[3].text: Der Eintritt kostet acht Euro, aber mit Studentenausweis nur vier. A price question is often answered after aber. Wait for the whole sentence before you write the number.
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: Admission costs eight euros, but with a student card only four.
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: Oh, and please bring your student card!
help.tips[3].check.q: You hear: „Die Karte kostet zwölf Euro, aber für Kinder nur sechs.“ How much does a child pay?
help.tips[3].check.why: The first price is changed by aber: for children it is only sechs Euro.
help.remember[0]: weil … ist: the last word closes the reason.
help.remember[1]: Treffen wir uns …? = shall we meet …? — the meeting place follows in the dative.
help.exam: Voicemails like this are a standard listening text in the A2 exam — and on your own phone almost every week.
help.hook: Catch every detail of a friend's voicemail — what, when, where to meet, and what it really costs once you hear aber.
passageTranslation: Hi Lisa, it's me, Jan. I wanted to ask whether you have time on Saturday. There is a new exhibition at the art museum – photos of Berlin in the 1920s. I think you'll like it, because you're so interested in photography. We can go at three o'clock, because it's not so crowded then. In the morning there are always lots of school classes. Admission costs eight euros, but with a student card only four. Afterwards maybe we'll have a coffee in the café next to the museum – they have the best cake in town. Shall we meet at a quarter to three in front of the museum? Or shall I pick you up by car? Please call me back, or send me a message. Oh, and please bring your student card! See you Saturday, bye!
questions[0].explanation: "… eine neue Ausstellung im Kunstmuseum – Fotos aus Berlin in den zwanziger Jahren."
questions[0].questionTranslation: What kind of exhibition is at the museum?
questions[1].explanation: "Wir können um drei Uhr hingehen, weil es dann nicht so voll ist." The price is the same all day.
questions[1].questionTranslation: Why does Jan want to go at three?
questions[1].optionsTranslation[1]: because he works in the morning
questions[2].explanation: "Der Eintritt kostet acht Euro, aber mit Studentenausweis nur vier."
questions[2].questionTranslation: How much is admission for students?
questions[3].explanation: "Treffen wir uns um Viertel vor drei vor dem Museum?" The café comes afterwards.
questions[3].questionTranslation: Where do they want to meet?
questions[3].optionsTranslation[0]: in the café next to the museum
questions[4].explanation: "… und bring bitte deinen Studentenausweis mit!"
questions[5].explanation: "Treffen wir uns um Viertel vor drei vor dem Museum?"
questions[5].questionTranslation: When does Jan want to meet Lisa?
